source_claims.statement: Started with known historical SSRF endpoints (druid/indexer/v1/task, v2/sql referencing CVE-2023-0361). Both failed due to missing configuration.
After failures, explored Druid console for extensions/plugins; proxy endpoint produced an error indicating SSRF potential. Iterative attacks succeeded.

research_questions.formulation: After known SSRF endpoints are unavailable due to configuration, does the management console expose an alternative proxy or extension path that can reach internal resources?
research_questions.anchor: shift to console after task/sql failures
research_questions.uncertainty_reduced: existence and exploitability of console proxy
research_questions.assumption_challenged: that historical SSRF locations are the only relevant ones

environment_model_updates: Known SSRF endpoints not configured on this instance
Console proxy endpoint exists and is reachable

systematic_vs_exploratory.systematic: testing of previously documented SSRF locations
systematic_vs_exploratory.exploratory: guessing console extensions after systematic options failed

negative_inconclusive: v2/sql: failed due to configuration (blocked prerequisite, not falsified SSRF class)

forbidden_inferences: Process is thin; do not invent detailed experiment sequence beyond the high-level pivot described

layer_b_candidate_principles: When historical attack surface is unavailable due to configuration, examine adjacent management or console surfaces before abandoning the direction

model_vs_harness: Recall of historical CVEs is model knowledge; systematic enumeration of known endpoints and logging of configuration-related failures can be harness.
